svg.text: FIGURE 7: INCANDESCENT BULBS & INSTRUMENT LOADING DECISION ENGINE
Rated vs Operating Power, Series/Parallel Brightness & Fuse Hierarchy, Voltmeter/Ammeter Extension & Loading Errors

g.text: 1. Incandescent Bulb Rated Physics
Printed Rating Specifications (V_R, P_R)
• Every bulb is manufactured with a nominal design rating: (V_rated, P_rated).
Example: 220 V, 100 W bulb.
Inherent Filament Hot Resistance R:
R = ( V_rated )² / P_rated
★ FUNDAMENTAL INVERSE SCALING LAW:
Higher rated wattage ⟹ LOWER filament resistance! (R ∝ 1 / P_rated).
Rated Current vs. Actual Operating Quantities
1. Rated Nominal Current I_rated:
I_rated = P_rated / V_rated = V_rated / R
Maximum safe continuous current before filament melts / fuses!
2. Actual Operating Power P_actual (Brightness Driver):
P_actual = I_actual² · R = ( V_actual )² / R
★ GOLDEN RULE FOR BULB BRIGHTNESS:
The brightness of a bulb is SOLELY DETERMINED by the ACTUAL power
dissipated P_actual under real circuit conditions, NOT the printed label!
Tungsten Filament Non-Linearity & Cold Inrush
• Tungsten has a strong Positive Temperature Coefficient (PTC):
R_hot ≈ 10 to 12 × R_cold (at T_hot ≈ 2500 K)
Cold Inrush Current Transient:
I_inrush = V_supply / R_cold ≈ 10 × I_rated !
• Why bulbs almost ALWAYS blow at the moment of turning ON!
• Thermal time constant τ_thermal ≈ 50 - 100 ms as filament heats up.
• In standard GATE problems (unless stated otherwise), treat R as constant.
Worked Resistance Hierarchy Example
Consider three bulbs rated at 220 V: 100 W (B₁), 60 W (B₂), 40 W (B₃):
Resistance Order: R_40W (1210 Ω) > R_60W (806 Ω) > R_100W (484 Ω)
The bulb with lowest wattage has the largest internal resistance!
Remember this order: it completely inverts in series connections!
2. Series / Parallel Bulbs & Fuse Hazards
Case A: Parallel Connection Across Rated Supply V_R
• All bulbs share the SAME supply voltage: V_actual = V_rated.
Actual Power Dissipated:
P_actual = V_R² / R = P_rated (Operates at full rating!)
★ Brightness Ranking in Parallel:
100 W > 60 W > 40 W (Higher Rated Bulb Glows Brighter!)
• Total power consumed: P_total = P₁ + P₂ + P₃ = 100 + 60 + 40 = 200 W.
• If one bulb burns out, the remaining bulbs continue glowing unchanged.
Case B: Series Connection Across Rated Supply V_R
• All bulbs share the SAME series current: I = V_R / (R₁ + R₂ + R₃).
Actual Power Dissipated: P_actual = I² · R ∝ R
★ Brightness Ranking in Series:
40 W > 60 W > 100 W (LOWER Rated Bulb Glows Brighter!)
Since current is identical, the bulb with LARGEST resistance drops the
highest voltage and dissipates the maximum power!
• Total power consumed in series: P_total = 1 / (1/P₁ + 1/P₂ + 1/P₃) ≪ P_parallel.
★ Case C: Excess Supply Voltage & Fusing Threshold
• What happens if two bulbs are connected in series across an EXCESS
voltage supply V_supply > V_rated (e.g. 440 V across two 220 V bulbs)?
Voltage Division Across Bulbs B₁ (100W) and B₂ (40W):
V_40W (314.3 V) ≫ V_rated (220 V) ⇒ 40 W BULB FUSES FIRST!
Immediate Post-Fuse System State:
• Once the 40 W bulb fuses, its filament breaks (Open Circuit, i = 0 A).
• The 100 W bulb is saved from burning out, but immediately TURNS OFF!
• Terminal voltage across the burnt 40 W bulb rises to full 440 V!
Master Fuse Identification Rule
When arbitrary rated bulbs are connected in series across high voltage:
1. Calculate rated current for each: I_R,k = P_R,k / V_R,k.
2. The bulb with the LOWEST rated current I_R will fuse first!
3. For identical voltage ratings: Bulb with LOWEST wattage fuses first!
• Maximum safe supply voltage without fusing any bulb:
V_max = min(I_R,k) · ( R₁ + R₂ + ... + R_n )
3. Meter Range Extension Analytics
Basic PMMC Meter Movement
• Permanent Magnet Moving Coil (PMMC): Deflection θ ∝ I_m (pure DC average!).
• Meter Parameters: Internal coil resistance R_m, Full-Scale Current I_fsd.
Full-Scale Voltage Drop V_m = I_fsd · R_m
• Typical values: I_fsd = 50 μA to 1 mA; R_m = 50 Ω to 2000 Ω.
• To measure larger currents or voltages, external resistors must be added.
★ Ideal Ammeter: R_A = 0 Ω | Ideal Voltmeter: R_V = ∞ Ω.
Ammeter Extension: Shunt Resistor R_sh
• Connect a small resistance R_sh in PARALLEL with meter movement.
Multiplying Power m = I / I_fsd:
Total current I splits into I_fsd through coil and (I - I_fsd) through shunt:
I_fsd · R_m = ( I - I_fsd ) · R_sh
R_sh = R_m / ( m - 1 ) [m = I / I_fsd]
• Material: Manganin (near-zero temperature coefficient α ≈ 0).
• Swamping Resistor: Small copper/manganin series resistor with meter coil
to minimize temperature-induced measurement errors.
• Aryton / Universal Multi-Range Shunt eliminates switch contact resistance.
Voltmeter Extension: Series Multiplier R_se
• Connect a large resistance R_se in SERIES with meter movement.
Voltage Multiplying Power m = V / V_m:
Total voltage V divides across R_se and meter coil R_m:
V = I_fsd · ( R_m + R_se )
R_se = R_m · ( m - 1 ) [m = V / V_m]
• Notice the beautiful mathematical duality between shunt and series multiplier:
Ammeter: R_sh = R_m / (m - 1) ⟷ Voltmeter: R_se = R_m · (m - 1)
• Material: Constantan or Manganin wire non-inductively wound.
Voltmeter Sensitivity S (Ohms-per-Volt)
• Figures of Merit: Reciprocal of full-scale deflection current:
S = 1 / I_fsd [Units: Ω / V]
Internal Voltmeter Resistance on Range V_range:
R_v = S · V_range
• Example: If S = 20,000 Ω/V on 10 V range ⇒ R_v = 20,000 × 10 = 200 kΩ.
On 50 V range ⇒ R_v = 20,000 × 50 = 1 MΩ.
★ HIGHER sensitivity ⟹ HIGHER internal resistance ⟹ LOWER loading error!
4. Loading Errors & Master Decision Tree
Voltmeter Loading Effect Analytics
• When voltmeter with finite R_v is connected across load resistor R_L:
Effective Resistance = R_L ∥ R_v = (R_L · R_v) / (R_L + R_v) < R_L
• True open-circuit voltage: V_true = V_th · [ R_L / (R_th + R_L) ]
• Measured loaded voltage: V_meas = V_th · [ (R_L ∥ R_v) / (R_th + R_L ∥ R_v) ] < V_true
Percentage Voltmeter Loading Error ε_v:
ε_v = [ (V_meas - V_true) / V_true ] × 100 % < 0
• To keep loading error < 1%: Ensure R_v ≥ 100 × ( R_th ∥ R_L )!
Ammeter Insertion Loading Effect Analytics
• Ammeter with internal resistance R_A inserted into loop with R_total:
I_true = V_th / R_total | I_meas = V_th / ( R_total + R_A )
Percentage Ammeter Insertion Error ε_A:
• Always under-reads current because insertion adds unwanted series impedance.
• To keep error < 1%: Ensure R_A ≤ 0.01 × R_total!
★ MASTER EXAM 4-TRACK RAPID DECISION ENGINE
When you encounter ANY Network Analysis problem in GATE 2027:
TRACK A: Power, Energy & Conservation (Tellegen / PSC)
1. Identify reference current direction w.r.t positive terminal.
2. Current enters (+) ⇒ P_abs = +v·i. Current leaves (+) ⇒ P_del = +v·i.
3. Multi-source power: Never sum power directly! Calculate i_total first: P = (i₁ ± i₂)² R.
4. Check Tellegen power balance: ∑ P_del ≡ ∑ P_abs across all elements.
TRACK B: Systematic Circuit Formulation (Nodal vs Mesh)
1. Count nodes n and branches b. Compare (n - 1) vs (b - n + 1).
2. Non-planar graph? Nodal analysis is MANDATORY (Mesh impossible!).
3. Floating voltage source? Form Supernode (outer KCL + inner KVL constraint).
4. Shared current source? Form Supermesh (outer KVL + inner current constraint).
TRACK C: Reductions & High-Order Symmetry
1. Look for Wheatstone bridge: Test R₁ R₄ == R₂ R₃. If equal, snip detector!
2. Test Folding symmetry: Mirror nodes have equal V ⇒ snip cross-branches or fold.
3. Test Perpendicular symmetry: Current splits evenly ⇒ lift and split central nodes.
4. 3D Cube: Recall Edge (7/12 R) < Face (3/4 R) < Body Diagonal (5/6 R).
TRACK D: Bulbs & Measuring Instrument Loading
1. Bulbs: Find R = V_R² / P_R. In parallel, higher W glows brighter.
2. Bulbs in series: LOWER W glows brighter! Under high voltage, lowest W fuses first!
3. Ammeter shunt: R_sh = R_m / (m - 1). Voltmeter series: R_se = R_m · (m - 1).
4. Loading error: Always negative. S = 1/I_fsd; higher sensitivity minimizes error.
